title: Nasdaq Posts Record Daily Close of 27,477 on AI Rally

tickers.name: Meta Platforms, Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
Nvidia's 2% gain pushed its market valuation above $5.7 trillion and led the Nasdaq Composite to a record closing price of 27,477.31 on Oct. 5. The rally added $540 billion to the US stock market, while the S&P 500 climbed 0.7% to finish just 0.5% below its own all-time high. Gains in Microsoft, Meta, and Tesla further bolstered the tech-heavy index, which broke out of a 4 month trading range.

The record close occurred despite US 20 year and 30 year Treasury yields hitting 24 year highs and an ISM Services PMI reading that came in lower than expected. Investors focused on the long term benefits of artificial intelligence to override rising borrowing costs, with Interactive Brokers strategist Steve Sosnick noting that AI benefits are viewed by some as essentially infinite. Analysts now question whether higher financing costs will eventually slow AI investment for smaller companies unable to absorb the expense.

AI OPTIMISM OVERRIDES RISING BOND YIELDS

Tech stocks are rallying even as bond yields climb, with investors continuing to bet heavily on the long-term benefits of AI.

Interactive Brokers strategist Steve Sosnick summed up the mood: “If you think the benefits of AI are essentially infinite, so what if you have to pay more to borrow money?”

selectedTweets.text:
🇺🇸 Wall Street keeps climbing

The Nasdaq hit another record, Nvidia gained 2% and pushed past a $5.7 trillion valuation, while Microsoft, Meta and Tesla also finished higher.

The big question is whether higher bond yields eventually make borrowing expensive enough to slow the AI investment boom.

Big players like Nvidia, Microsoft, and Meta can probably absorb that.

Smaller companies may have a much harder time keeping up if financing gets more expensive.
